issues.legal_issue: Acquired land that forms one compact block should not be divided into categories without a justified basis.
material_facts: The Collector divided the acquired land into three categories based on its nature and quality in the revenue records.
The Supreme Court found no justification for dividing the acquired land into three groups and agreed with the lower courts that it should be treated as one compact block.
issues.conclusion: The land was properly treated as one compact block rather than divided into categories.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the case-specific principle that land forming one compact block should be valued together where there is no justification for categorizing it. No earlier cases or specific statutory provision were relied on for this conclusion; Sections 17 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act are mentioned as part of the acquisition and reference proceedings.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and compact_block and not justified_categorization

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.compact_block: The acquired land forms one compact block.
predicates.justified_categorization: The party seeking separate categories has a supported basis for dividing the land into those categories.

issues.definition: When an acquisition compensation appeal concerns land that forms one compact block and no supported basis exists for categorizing it, the land is assessed as one block.

issues.legal_issue: Market value of acquired land cannot be enhanced on the basis of non-comparable sale instances and non-expert oral evidence when reliable official valuation evidence supports a different value.
material_facts: The acquisition comprised a large tract of land.
The sale instances relied on by the claimants concerned small parcels of about three to four marlas; only one was proved, and it concerned a small parcel.
The Tehsildar, acting on a government official's request to investigate local prices, reported that the market price was Rs.30,000 per kanal.
The Tehsildar's report was admitted without objection and was not challenged by either appellant.
The lower courts enhanced the valuation to Rs.45,000 per kanal, relying mainly on sale instances the Supreme Court found non-comparable and on oral evidence from local witnesses who were not experts.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to compensation for the land at no more than Rs.30,000 per kanal, and the enhanced valuation of Rs.45,000 per kanal was modified.
issues.legal_principle: In determining market value, sale instances must be comparable to the acquired land in relevant respects, including the scale of the land being valued; non-expert oral evidence is not a sound basis for fixing market value. The Court relied on the admitted, unchallenged report of the Tehsildar as the evidence bearing on value. Sections 17 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act are mentioned in the account of the acquisition and reference proceedings, but no earlier cases or specific statutory valuation rule are cited.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and large_acquired_tract and small_noncomparable_sales and unchallenged_official_valuation_report

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.large_acquired_tract: The acquired land is a large tract whose value is being determined as a whole.
predicates.small_noncomparable_sales: The sale evidence concerns parcels too small or otherwise unsuitable to serve as comparable sales for the acquired tract.
predicates.unchallenged_official_valuation_report: A government official's valuation report is admitted without objection and is not challenged by the parties.

issues.definition: In an acquisition compensation appeal, when a large tract is supported by an unchallenged official valuation report but the sale evidence consists of non-comparable small parcels, the land value is fixed by the official valuation evidence.

issues.legal_issue: Separate compensation for fruit-bearing trees and tubewells may be upheld when the applicable government circular allows it and no contrary material is shown.
material_facts: The High Court relied on a government circular allowing separate compensation for fruit-bearing trees and tubewells.
Nothing contrary to the circular or the resulting finding was brought to the Supreme Court's notice.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to disturb the separate compensation awarded for fruit-bearing trees and tubewells.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld separate compensation on the basis of the applicable government circular and the absence of contrary material. No earlier cases or specific statutory provision were relied on for this conclusion; Sections 17 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act are mentioned as part of the acquisition and reference proceedings.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.government_circular_allows_separate_comp: A government circular allows compensation for an acquired asset separately from compensation for the land.
predicates.no_contrary_material: No material is brought forward that contradicts the circular or the separate compensation finding.

issues.definition: When a government circular allows separate compensation for an acquired asset and no contrary material is shown in an acquisition compensation appeal, the separate compensation is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A substantial costs award in a land acquisition compensation proceeding must be based on a judicial exercise of discretion.
material_facts: The District Judge awarded substantial costs to the claimants, and the High Court left that award undisturbed.
The Supreme Court found no justification for the substantial costs award and set aside the costs orders, while allowing usual costs prescribed by law proportionately.
issues.conclusion: The substantial costs awards were set aside; the parties remained entitled to usual costs prescribed by law proportionately.
issues.legal_principle: Discretion concerning costs must be exercised judicially. The Court relied on that principle without citing an earlier case or a specific statutory provision.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.substantial_costs_awarded: A court has awarded substantial costs to a party in the compensation proceeding.
predicates.no_judicial_justification: The record provides no justification for the substantial costs award.

issues.definition: When a substantial costs award in an acquisition compensation appeal lacks judicial justification, that award is set aside.
